scope: Genesis 1–11; all 299 verses. Chapters 12–50 are unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.

delta_method: F0 retained wording (punctuation may change); F1 wording; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive or textual choice. Editorial assessments, not similarity-generated classifications. All current wording and apparatus require editorial review.

verses.rationale: Retain the clear opening rather than force difference; note the possible dependent opening construction.
verses.before: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
verses.after: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

verses.rationale: Separate the scene-setting clauses; retain the Spirit reading while noting wind/breath and the open force of the Hebrew phrase.
verses.before: And the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters.
verses.after: The earth was unformed and empty. Darkness lay over the deep, and God's Spirit hovered over the waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters.

verses.rationale: Keep speech and its immediate realization in one audible sentence.
verses.before: God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
verses.after: Then God said, “Let there be light,” and light came to be.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

verses.rationale: Join evaluation and separation naturally without removing their sequence.
verses.before: God saw that the light was good. And God separated the light from the darkness.
verses.after: God saw that the light was good and separated the light from the darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God saw that the light was good. And God separated the light from the darkness.

verses.rationale: Retain naming and the recurring evening/morning rhythm; preserve the cardinal one rather than silently making it ordinal.
verses.before: God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
verses.after: God named the light Day and the darkness Night. Evening came, and morning came: day one.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.

verses.rationale: Render raqia as dome, keeping the ancient picture of divided waters; record expanse/vault alternatives.
verses.before: God said, “Let there be an expanse among the waters, and let it separate the waters from the waters.”
verses.after: God said, “Let there be a dome between the waters, separating water from water.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it separate the waters from the waters.”

verses.rationale: Make spatial referents explicit while keeping both upper and lower waters.
verses.before: God made the expanse and separated the waters that were under the expanse from the waters that were above the expanse. And it was so.
verses.after: God made the dome and separated the water beneath it from the water above it. And so it was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God made the expanse and separated the waters that were under the expanse from the waters that were above the expanse. And it was so.

verses.rationale: Use sky for the named dome; retain the chapter's naming and time refrain.
verses.before: God called the expanse Heavens. And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.
verses.after: God named the dome Sky. Evening came, and morning came: the second day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God called the expanse Heavens. And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.

verses.rationale: Use concrete English for gathering and appearing; preserve the single gathering place.
verses.before: God said, “Let the waters under the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so.
verses.after: God said, “Let the water beneath the sky gather in one place, and let dry ground appear.” And so it was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let the waters under the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so.

verses.rationale: Keep both named domains and the approval refrain.
verses.before: God called the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
verses.after: God named the dry ground Land and the gathered waters Seas. God saw that it was good.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God called the dry land Earth, and the gathered waters he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.

verses.rationale: Unfold the vegetation categories and seed-bearing function without substituting modern biological classifications.
verses.before: God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: plants yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind, upon the earth.” And it was so.
verses.after: God said, “Let the land grow vegetation: plants that produce seed and fruit trees that bear fruit with seed in it, each of its own kind, on the land.” And so it was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: plants yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind, upon the earth.” And it was so.

verses.rationale: Keep the realized command parallel to 1:11 and retain both plant and tree categories.
verses.before: And the earth brought forth vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kinds, and trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.after: The land grew vegetation: plants producing seed of their own kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed in it, each of its own kind. God saw that it was good.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the earth brought forth vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kinds, and trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

verses.rationale: Keep the chosen refrain consistent across creation days rather than vary it for novelty.
verses.before: And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.
verses.after: Evening came, and morning came: the third day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.

verses.rationale: Break the functions into readable clauses; preserve appointed times rather than reducing them to modern seasons alone.
verses.before: God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate the day from the night. And let them be for signs and for appointed times, and for days and years,
verses.after: God said, “Let lights appear in the dome of the sky to separate day from night. Let them serve as signs and mark appointed times, days, and years.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate the day from the night. And let them be for signs and for appointed times, and for days and years,

subsequent_editorial_changes.previous_after: God said, “Let lights appear in the dome of the sky to separate day from night. Let them mark signs, appointed times, days, and years.
subsequent_editorial_changes.rationale: The lights are to be signs (le-otot), not to mark signs. Give the sign function natural English while retaining the appointed times, days and years.

verses.rationale: Carry the speech across the verse boundary and keep the lights' earthly function.
verses.before: and let them be lights in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth.” And it was so.
verses.after: Let them shine in the dome of the sky to give light to the earth.” And so it was.
verses.tsw_comparator: and let them be lights in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth.” And it was so.

verses.rationale: Retain functional larger/smaller descriptions without substituting sun and moon into the main text.
verses.before: God made the two great lights—the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night—and the stars.
verses.after: God made the two great lights: the larger light to rule the day and the smaller light to rule the night. God made the stars too.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God made the two great lights—the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night—and the stars.

verses.rationale: Keep the placement and purpose connected to the following verse.
verses.before: God set them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
verses.after: God placed them in the dome of the sky to shine on the earth,
verses.tsw_comparator: And God set them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,

verses.rationale: Preserve all three light functions and the evaluation.
verses.before: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
verses.after: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God saw that it was good.
verses.tsw_comparator: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

verses.rationale: Retain the same day refrain and ordinal number.
verses.before: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.
verses.after: Evening came, and morning came: the fourth day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.

verses.rationale: Render the swarm idiom naturally while preserving both water and flying life.
verses.before: God said, “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the heavens.”
verses.after: God said, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the dome of the sky.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the heavens.”

verses.rationale: Preserve great creatures, abundant moving life, and kinds without identifying a modern species.
verses.before: God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarm, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.after: God created the great sea creatures and all the living things that move and teem in the waters, each of its own kind, and every kind of winged bird. God saw that it was good.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarm, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

verses.rationale: Retain blessing and reproductive commands while separating the bird clause.
verses.before: God blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
verses.after: God blessed them: “Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the waters of the seas. Let the birds multiply on the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And God blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”

verses.rationale: Retain the same day refrain and ordinal number.
verses.before: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.
verses.after: Evening came, and morning came: the fifth day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.

verses.rationale: Use accessible animal categories without erasing the repeated kinds formula.
verses.before: God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock and creeping things and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.
verses.after: God said, “Let the land produce living creatures of every kind: livestock, creatures that crawl, and wild animals, each of its own kind.” And so it was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock and creeping things and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.

verses.rationale: Maintain the repeated categories and the sequence of evaluation.
verses.before: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that creeps on the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.after: God made every kind of wild animal, every kind of livestock, and every kind of creature that crawls on the ground. God saw that it was good.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that creeps on the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

verses.rationale: Keep unexplained us/our, collective humanity, and rule; do not replace dominion with an interpretive stewardship paraphrase.
verses.before: God said, “Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness. And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”
verses.after: God said, “Let us make humanity in our image, in our likeness. Let them rule the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, the whole earth, and every creature that crawls on it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness. And let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over the livestock and over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”

subsequent_editorial_changes.previous_after: God said, “Let us make humanity in our image, to bear our likeness. Let them rule the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, the whole earth, and every creature that crawls on it.”
subsequent_editorial_changes.rationale: Ke-dmutenu describes likeness. Remove the purpose construction to bear, which can suggest an additional stated purpose; retain image and likeness as distinct expressions.

verses.rationale: Retain the poetic three lines and collective referent; note the Hebrew singular-to-plural movement rather than turning humanity into a male-only group.
verses.before: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.
verses.after: God created humanity in his image; in God's image he created them; male and female he created them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.

verses.rationale: Keep subdue and rule in their force while presenting a readable sequence of commands.
verses.before: God blessed them. And God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
verses.after: God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Rule the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and every living creature that moves on the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And God blessed them. And God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”

verses.rationale: Make the gift and its purpose audible; preserve all plants/trees rather than generalizing to food alone.
verses.before: God said, “Look, I have given you every plant yielding seed that is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. They will be for you for food.
verses.after: God said, “Look, I give you every seed-producing plant on all the earth and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. These will be your food.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “Behold, I have given you every plant yielding seed that is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed-bearing fruit. They shall be for you for food.

verses.rationale: Retain the broad living-creature scope; do not retain the previous apparatus's incorrect neshama headword for this verse.
verses.before: And to every beast of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to everything that creeps on the earth, everything in which is the breath of life, I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.
verses.after: To every wild animal, every bird in the sky, and every creature that crawls on the earth—everything that has life in it—I give green plants for food.” And so it was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And to every beast of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to everything that creeps on the earth, everything in which is the breath of life, I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.

verses.rationale: Keep the heightened very good and final refrain without adding a scientific or doctrinal account.
verses.before: God saw everything that he had made, and look, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.
verses.after: God looked at everything that God had made: it was very good. Evening came, and morning came: the sixth day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.

verses.rationale: Render all their host as the full contents rather than an unexplained military term here.
verses.before: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.
verses.after: So the heavens and the earth were completed, with everything in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host.

verses.rationale: Retain the pinned Hebrew’s seventh-day completion and the connection between finishing and resting.
verses.before: And on the seventh day God finished the work that God had done, and rested on the seventh day from all the work that God had done.
verses.after: On the seventh day God completed the work and rested from all the work God had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: And on the seventh day God finished the work that God had done, and rested on the seventh day from all the work that God had done.

verses.rationale: Reduce repeated relative clauses while keeping blessing, holiness, rest, and creation.
verses.before: So God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it God rested from all the work of creating that God had done.
verses.after: God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on that day God rested from all the work of creation.
verses.tsw_comparator: So God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it God rested from all the work of creating that God had done.

verses.rationale: Keep the whole Hebrew verse under v04, including its second clause; preserve reversed earth/heaven order in the new scene.
verses.before: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created. On the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens,
verses.after: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created. When the LORD God made earth and heaven,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created. On the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens,

verses.rationale: Unfold the long scene-setting syntax without harmonizing its sequence with chapter 1.
verses.before: when no plant of the field was yet in the earth and no herb of the field had yet sprung up—for the LORD God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was no human to till the ground,
verses.after: no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant of the field had sprouted, because the LORD God had not sent rain on the earth and there was no human to work the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: when no plant of the field was yet in the earth and no herb of the field had yet sprung up—for the LORD God had not caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was no human to till the ground,

subsequent_editorial_changes.previous_after: no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant of the field had sprouted. The LORD God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no human to work the ground.
subsequent_editorial_changes.rationale: Make the explicit ki connection audible: the lack of rain and a human cultivator explains the preceding situation. The sentence still continues the temporal clause in 2:4.

verses.rationale: Use flow of water for the uncertain ed; note mist/stream possibilities rather than assert a modern hydrological mechanism.
verses.before: but a stream would rise from the earth and water the whole face of the ground—
verses.after: But a flow of water rose from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: but a stream would rise from the earth and water the whole face of the ground—

verses.rationale: Keep dust, shaping, divine breath, and living being; remove the depersonalizing its while explaining adam/adamah in a note.
verses.before: then the LORD God formed the human from the dust of the ground, and breathed into its nostrils the breath of life; and the human became a living being.
verses.after: The LORD God shaped the human from dust taken from the ground and breathed the breath of life into the human's nostrils. The human became a living being.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the LORD God formed the human from the dust of the ground, and breathed into its nostrils the breath of life; and the human became a living being.

verses.rationale: Use a clear locative referent while retaining the relative clause linking the human to God’s forming.
verses.before: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east; and there God put the human whom God had formed.
verses.after: The LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and placed there the human God had formed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east; and there God put the human whom God had formed.

verses.rationale: Split the tree description from the named trees; retain beauty because the source describes visual desirability.
verses.before: Out of the ground the LORD God made to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food, with the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.after: The LORD God made all kinds of trees grow from the ground, beautiful to look at and good for food. In the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Out of the ground the LORD God made to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food, with the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

verses.rationale: Keep the outward flow and fourfold division without inventing a geographical identification.
verses.before: A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides and becomes four branches.
verses.after: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden. From there, the river divided into four branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides and becomes four branches.

subsequent_editorial_changes.previous_after: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden. Beyond it, the river divided into four branches.
subsequent_editorial_changes.rationale: U-misham means and/from there. Avoid specifying beyond the garden where the source gives a less specific deictic expression.

verses.rationale: Make the name and location readable in two clauses while retaining the gold reference.
verses.before: The name of the first is the Pishon; it flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
verses.after: The first river was named Pishon. It wound through all the land of Havilah, where there was gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the first is the Pishon; it flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;

verses.rationale: Retain the precious materials with their uncertain identifications addressed in the note.
verses.before: and the gold of that land is good; bdellium and onyx stone are there.
verses.after: The gold of that land was good. Bdellium and onyx were found there too.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the gold of that land is good; bdellium and onyx stone are there.

verses.rationale: Parallel the first river sentence without identifying Cush with a modern state.
verses.before: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it flows around the whole land of Cush.
verses.after: The second river was named Gihon. It wound through all the land of Cush.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it flows around the whole land of Cush.

verses.rationale: Preserve order and location; use the recognizable river names with the Hebrew names in a note.
verses.before: The name of the third river is the Tigris, which flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
verses.after: The third river was the Tigris, flowing east of Assyria. The fourth was the Euphrates.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the third river is the Tigris, which flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

verses.rationale: Preserve work and keeping as two responsibilities; retain human as the designation with a coherent personal pronoun.
verses.before: The LORD God took the human and put the human in the garden of Eden to till it and to keep it.
verses.after: The LORD God took the human and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and care for it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD God took the human and put the human in the garden of Eden to till it and to keep it.

verses.rationale: Keep generous permission and its continuation into the prohibition.
verses.before: And the LORD God commanded the human, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;
verses.after: The LORD God commanded the human, “You may eat freely from every tree in the garden,
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD God commanded the human, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;

verses.rationale: Use natural command language and preserve emphatic death; note the literal in-the-day construction.
verses.before: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you will not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you will surely die.”
verses.after: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. When you eat from it, you will certainly die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.”

verses.rationale: Retain help and correspondence without loading either subordination or a complete theory of equality into the main text.
verses.before: Then the LORD God said, “It is not good that the human should be alone; I will make for the human a helper as a counterpart.”
verses.after: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the human to be alone. I will make him a helper who corresponds to him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD God said, “It is not good that the human should be alone; I will make for the human a helper as a counterpart.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the naming subject and split the result; retain formed rather than use had formed to force chronology.
verses.before: So out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to the human to see what the human would call them; and whatever the human called each living creature, that was its name.
verses.after: The LORD God formed every wild animal and every bird in the sky from the ground and brought them to the human to see what he would call them. Whatever he called each living creature became its name.
verses.tsw_comparator: So out of the ground the LORD God formed every animal of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to the human to see what the human would call them; and whatever the human called each living creature, that was its name.

verses.rationale: Keep all categories and the absence that drives the scene forward.
verses.before: The human gave names to all cattle, and to the birds of the air, and to every animal of the field; but for the human no helper as a counterpart was found.
verses.after: The human named all the livestock, the birds in the sky, and every wild animal. But no helper corresponding to him was found for the human.
verses.tsw_comparator: The human gave names to all cattle, and to the birds of the air, and to every animal of the field; but for the human no helper as a counterpart was found.

verses.rationale: Retain side with rib as an alternative in the note; preserve deep sleep and closure without anatomy invented beyond the text.
verses.before: So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the human, and the human slept; then God took one of its sides and closed up the place with flesh.
verses.after: The LORD God put the human into a deep sleep. While he slept, God took one of his sides and closed the flesh over the place.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the human, and the human slept; then God took one of its sides and closed up the place with flesh.

verses.rationale: Keep the unusual built verb and the act of bringing rather than smoothing away the literary image.
verses.before: And the side that the LORD God had taken from the human God built into a woman, and brought her to the human.
verses.after: The LORD God built the side taken from the human into a woman and brought her to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the side that the LORD God had taken from the human God built into a woman, and brought her to the human.

verses.rationale: Restore ish/ishah as Man/Woman in the wordplay; keep all speech inside v23's paragraph and distinguish these terms from adam.
verses.before: Then the human said, “This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; this one will be called Woman, for out of Human this one was taken.”
verses.after: The human said, “At last! Bone from my bones, and flesh from my flesh. She will be called Woman, because she was taken from Man.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the human said, “This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; this one shall be called Woman, for out of Human this one was taken.”

verses.rationale: Translate the explicit man/wife terms in this sentence rather than generic human/woman; retain the one-flesh image.
verses.before: So a human leaves father and mother and clings to a woman, and they become one flesh.
verses.after: That is why a man leaves his father and mother, holds fast to his wife, and they become one flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore a human leaves father and mother and clings to a woman, and they become one flesh.

verses.rationale: Retain the couple and absence of shame in natural personal English.
verses.before: And the two of them were naked, the human and the woman, and they were not ashamed.
verses.after: The human and his wife were both naked, and neither felt ashamed.

verses.after: Enoch was 65 years old when he became the father of Methuselah.

verses.rationale: Retain the stated total without adding the death refrain absent here.

verses.tsw_comparator: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him.

verses.rationale: Preserve Methuselah/Lamech and 187 years.
verses.before: When Methuselah had lived one hundred eighty-seven years, he fathered Lamech.
verses.after: Methuselah was 187 years old when he became the father of Lamech.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Methuselah had lived one hundred eighty-seven years, he fathered Lamech.

verses.before: Methuselah lived after he fathered Lamech seven hundred eighty-two years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

verses.tsw_comparator: Methuselah lived after he fathered Lamech seven hundred eighty-two years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Preserve 969 rather than rationalizing the lifespan.
verses.before: Thus all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, and he died.
verses.after: Methuselah lived 969 years in all. Then he died.

verses.rationale: Keep son unnamed until the naming verse and retain 182 years.
verses.before: When Lamech had lived one hundred eighty-two years, he fathered a son.
verses.after: Lamech was 182 years old when he became the father of a son.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Lamech had lived one hundred eighty-two years, he fathered a son.

verses.rationale: Preserve the naming explanation and work/pain/ground link to chapter 3, with the imperfect sound correspondence noted.

verses.after: He named him Noah, saying, “He will bring us relief from our work and the painful labor of our hands on the ground the LORD has cursed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he called his name Noah, saying, “This one will comfort us from our work and from the painful labor of our hands because of the ground that the LORD has cursed.”

verses.rationale: Preserve 595 subsequent years and the offspring formula.
verses.before: Lamech lived after he fathered Noah five hundred ninety-five years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.after: After Noah's birth, Lamech lived another 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lamech lived after he fathered Noah five hundred ninety-five years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Preserve the Masoretic 777-year total and the death refrain.
verses.before: Thus all the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy-seven years, and he died.
