verses.rationale: Treat the age statement as introducing the sons, not a claim of triplets; record the compressed genealogy syntax.
verses.before: After Noah was five hundred years old, Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.after: Noah was 500 years old, and he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.tsw_comparator: After Noah was five hundred years old, Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

subsequent_editorial_changes.previous_after: After Noah reached 500 years of age, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
subsequent_editorial_changes.rationale: Preserve the age statement and coordinated fatherhood statement without adding after. Do not harmonize the wording to a calculated chronology or imply that the three births were simultaneous.

verses.rationale: Keep the growing human population and daughters as the setting for the next verse.
verses.before: When humankind began to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them,
verses.after: As humans began to multiply across the ground, daughters were born to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When humankind began to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters were born to them,

verses.rationale: Retain sons of God without identifying them as angels or kings in the main text; keep unilateral choosing and source-described beauty.
verses.before: the sons of God saw that the daughters of humankind were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves from any whom they chose.
verses.after: The sons of God saw that the human daughters were beautiful, and they took as wives any they chose.
verses.tsw_comparator: the sons of God saw that the daughters of humankind were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves from any whom they chose.

verses.rationale: Retain remain with contend/judge alternatives and the disputed scope of 120 years in the note.
verses.before: Then the LORD said, “My spirit will not contend with humankind forever, for they are flesh; their days will be one hundred twenty years.”
verses.after: The LORD said, “My spirit will not remain in humans forever, for they are flesh. Their days will be 120 years.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said, “My spirit shall not contend with humankind forever, for they are flesh; their days shall be one hundred twenty years.”

verses.rationale: Keep Nephilim untranslated and the temporal clauses intact; do not supply a speculative identity or genealogy beyond the statement.
verses.before: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and also afterward—when the sons of God went in to the daughters of humankind and they bore children to them. These were the mighty ones who were of old, men of renown.
verses.after: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and afterward too, when the sons of God had relations with human daughters, who bore them children. These were the mighty ones of long ago, men of renown.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and also afterward—when the sons of God went in to the daughters of humankind and they bore children to them. These were the mighty ones who were of old, men of renown.

verses.rationale: Separate observation from the sweeping assessment; retain its uncomfortable absoluteness.
verses.before: The LORD saw that the evil of humankind was great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of their heart was only evil continually.
verses.after: The LORD saw how great human evil had become on the earth. Every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil, all the time.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD saw that the evil of humankind was great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of their heart was only evil continually.

verses.rationale: Retain regret and grief as the divine response rather than replacing them with an explanation that denies the wording.
verses.before: And the LORD regretted that he had made humankind on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.
verses.after: The LORD regretted making humans on the earth and was deeply grieved at heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD regretted that he had made humankind on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.

verses.rationale: Preserve the full scope of destruction and repeated regret without sentimentalizing it.
verses.before: So the LORD said, “I will blot out from the face of the ground the humankind whom I have created—humanity and animals and creeping things and birds of the heavens—for I regret that I have made them.”
verses.after: The LORD said, “I will wipe the humans I created from the ground—humans along with livestock, crawling creatures, and birds in the sky. I regret having made them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD said, “I will blot out from the face of the ground the humankind whom I have created—humanity and animals and creeping things and birds of the heavens—for I regret that I have made them.”

verses.rationale: Retain the brief narrative contrast and favor image; no added explanation of merit.
verses.before: Yet Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: But Noah found favor in the LORD's eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Make the family formula and character description readable while retaining walked with God as an Enoch echo.
verses.before: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among his generation. Noah walked with God.
verses.after: This is the account of Noah's family. Noah was righteous and blameless among the people of his time. Noah walked with God.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among his generation. Noah walked with God.

verses.rationale: Preserve the explicit count and order of the named sons.
verses.before: Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.after: Noah became the father of three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

verses.rationale: Keep corruption and violence together, with the same corrupt root carried into the destruction warning.
verses.before: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and the earth was filled with violence.
verses.after: The earth was corrupt in God's sight, filled with violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and the earth was filled with violence.

verses.rationale: Retain all flesh and the repeated corruption rather than silently narrow the referent to one social group.
verses.before: God saw the earth, and look, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
verses.after: God looked at the earth: it was corrupt, because all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve all flesh, the causal violence claim, and the scope of destruction; note destroy as another use of the corrupt root.
verses.before: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. Therefore look, I am about to destroy them with the earth.
verses.after: God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before me, because the earth is filled with violence through them. I am about to destroy them along with the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. Therefore behold, I am about to destroy them with the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep the unidentified timber name and explain ark/compartments/pitch selectively; do not assert a wood species.
verses.before: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood. You will make rooms in the ark, and you will cover it inside and outside with pitch.
verses.after: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood. Build compartments in it, and coat it inside and out with pitch.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ark, and you shall cover it inside and outside with pitch.

verses.rationale: Retain all three dimensions and the ancient unit; explain cubit in the vocabulary.
verses.before: This is how you will make it: the length of the ark will be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
verses.after: Build it 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is how you shall make it: the length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.

verses.rationale: Choose roof for the uncertain tsohar construction with alternatives noted; retain cubit, side entrance, and three levels without claiming a complete blueprint.
verses.before: You will make a roof for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from above, and set the door of the ark in its side. You will make it with lower, second, and third decks.
verses.after: Make a roof for the ark, finishing it to within a cubit of the top. Put an entrance in its side, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall make a roof for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from above, and set the door of the ark in its side. You shall make it with lower, second, and third decks.

verses.rationale: Retain the emphatic divine agency, breath, all-flesh scope, and final death statement.
verses.before: For look, I am bringing the floodwaters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life under the heavens. Everything that is on the earth will perish.
verses.after: I am bringing floodwaters over the earth to destroy all flesh under the heavens that has the breath of life in it. Everything on the earth will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: For behold, I am bringing the floodwaters upon the earth to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life under the heavens. Everything that is on the earth shall perish.

verses.rationale: Separate covenant from entering while retaining every family group and the contrast with destruction.
verses.before: Yet I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
verses.after: But I will establish my covenant with you. Enter the ark with your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.

verses.rationale: Make the preservation purpose explicit and retain the paired sexes.
verses.before: And from every living thing of all flesh, you will bring two of every kind into the ark to keep them alive with you; they will be male and female.
verses.after: Bring two of every kind of living creature into the ark to keep them alive with you, a male and a female.
verses.tsw_comparator: And from every living thing of all flesh, you shall bring two of every kind into the ark to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.

verses.rationale: Retain kinds, approach to Noah, and the purpose without collapsing it into his action in the previous verse.
verses.before: Of the birds according to their kinds, and of the animals according to their kinds, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of every kind will come to you to keep them alive.
verses.after: Two of every kind of bird, livestock, and creature that crawls on the ground will come to you to be kept alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: Of the birds according to their kinds, and of the animals according to their kinds, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of every kind shall come to you to keep them alive.

verses.rationale: Keep food gathering, storage, and its shared human/nonhuman destination.
verses.before: And you will take with you every kind of food that is eaten and gather it to yourself, and it will be food for you and for them.”
verses.after: Gather and store every kind of food that can be eaten. It will be food for you and for them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall take with you every kind of food that is eaten and gather it to yourself, and it shall be food for you and for them.”

verses.rationale: Preserve emphatic repeated obedience in two natural sentences.
verses.before: Noah did this; according to all that God commanded him, so he did.
verses.after: Noah did all of this. He did everything God commanded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Noah did this; according to all that God commanded him, so he did.

verses.rationale: Retain household and the evaluative comparison rather than add a general claim about the family.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.
verses.after: The LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark with your whole household. Among this generation, I have seen that you are righteous before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.

verses.rationale: Render seven-seven as pairs in view of the paired wording; retain clean/unclean distinction with alternatives and context in the note.
verses.before: From every clean animal you will take with you seven pairs, a male and its mate; and from the animals that are not clean, one pair, a male and its mate;
verses.after: Take seven pairs of every clean animal, each male with its mate, and one pair of every animal that is not clean, a male with its mate.
verses.tsw_comparator: From every clean animal you shall take with you seven pairs, a male and its mate; and from the animals that are not clean, one pair, a male and its mate;

verses.rationale: Retain the unqualified birds category and reproductive purpose; do not import clean into this verse.
verses.before: and from the birds of the heavens also, seven pairs, male and female, to keep their offspring alive upon the face of all the earth.
verses.after: Take seven pairs of the birds in the sky too, male and female, to keep their offspring alive across the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and from the birds of the heavens also, seven pairs, male and female, to keep their offspring alive upon the face of all the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain waiting time, rain duration, and destruction scope without merging different numbers in the narrative.
verses.before: For in seven days I will send rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out from the face of the ground every living thing that I have made.”
verses.after: In seven days I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe from the ground every living thing I have made.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For in seven days I will send rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out from the face of the ground every living thing that I have made.”

verses.rationale: Keep the clear obedience statement even where its wording overlaps; preserve LORD rather than substitute God indiscriminately.
verses.before: Noah did according to all that the LORD commanded him.
verses.after: Noah did everything the LORD commanded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Noah did according to all that the LORD commanded him.

verses.rationale: Preserve age and the temporal event without converting to a modern date.
verses.before: Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
verses.after: Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came over the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.

verses.rationale: Make the reason for entering natural while preserving all named family groups.
verses.before: Noah entered the ark with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives because of the waters of the flood.
verses.after: Noah went into the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives to escape the floodwaters.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Noah entered the ark with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives because of the waters of the flood.

verses.rationale: List the full categories while carrying the sentence into the paired-entry verse.
verses.before: From the clean animals and from the animals that were not clean, and from the birds and everything that creeps upon the ground,
verses.after: Clean animals and animals that were not clean, birds, and everything that crawls on the ground
verses.tsw_comparator: From the clean animals and from the animals that were not clean, and from the birds and everything that creeps upon the ground,

verses.rationale: Preserve arrival, pairs, sexes, and the obedience formula without harmonizing away the seven-pair instruction.
verses.before: two by two they went into the ark with Noah, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
verses.after: came to Noah in the ark two by two, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
verses.tsw_comparator: two by two they went into the ark with Noah, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.

verses.rationale: Make the backward time reference explicit and preserve the seven days.
verses.before: And after seven days the waters of the flood came upon the earth.
verses.after: After those seven days, the floodwaters came over the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And after seven days the waters of the flood came upon the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain every date component and the ancient upper/lower water images without meteorological replacement.
verses.before: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
verses.after: In the 600th year of Noah's life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens opened.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the windows of the heavens were opened.

verses.rationale: Retain the duration and natural repeated wording without trying to vary a simple statement artificially.
verses.before: And rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
verses.after: Rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
verses.tsw_comparator: And rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

verses.rationale: Preserve emphatic same-day entry, son names, and explicit three wives.
verses.before: On that very day Noah and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons entered the ark with them,
verses.after: That very day Noah entered the ark with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah's wife, and his sons' three wives.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that very day Noah and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons entered the ark with them,

verses.rationale: Keep the expansive repeated inventory and final winged emphasis.
verses.before: they and every animal according to its kind, and all the livestock according to their kinds, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every winged creature.
verses.after: With them were wild animals of every kind, livestock of every kind, every kind of creature that crawls on the earth, and birds of every kind—every bird, everything with wings.
verses.tsw_comparator: they and every animal according to its kind, and all the livestock according to their kinds, and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every winged creature.

verses.rationale: Preserve paired movement and the breath/all-flesh link.
verses.before: They went into the ark with Noah, two by two of all flesh in which was the breath of life.
verses.after: They came to Noah in the ark two by two, from all flesh that had the breath of life.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went into the ark with Noah, two by two of all flesh in which was the breath of life.

verses.rationale: Preserve the switch from God to LORD and the act of closing rather than assign it to Noah.
verses.before: And those that entered, male and female of all flesh, entered as God had commanded him. Then the LORD shut him in.
verses.after: A male and a female of every kind of flesh entered, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
verses.tsw_comparator: And those that entered, male and female of all flesh, entered as God had commanded him. Then the LORD shut him in.

verses.rationale: Separate duration and rising action while preserving the lifted-ark image.
verses.before: The flood continued forty days upon the earth. The waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth.
verses.after: For forty days the flood was on the earth. The waters rose, lifting the ark clear of the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: The flood continued forty days upon the earth. The waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep both strength and increase rather than only modern water level.
verses.before: The waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark floated upon the face of the waters.
verses.after: The waters grew stronger and rose higher over the earth, and the ark moved across their surface.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark floated upon the face of the waters.

verses.rationale: Retain the narrative's comprehensive claim without limiting or expanding its geography independently.
verses.before: The waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and all the high mountains under the whole heavens were covered.
verses.after: The waters grew stronger still, until every high mountain beneath the whole sky was covered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, and all the high mountains under the whole heavens were covered.

verses.rationale: Retain the conventional above-mountains attachment while flagging the compact measurement clause for review.
verses.before: The waters prevailed fifteen cubits above them, and the mountains were covered.
verses.after: The waters rose fifteen cubits above the mountains and covered them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters prevailed fifteen cubits above them, and the mountains were covered.

verses.rationale: Preserve every group and the total human loss; do not reduce the flood to a gentle animal story.
verses.before: And all flesh died that moved upon the earth: birds and livestock and animals and every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth, and all humankind.
verses.after: All flesh moving on the earth died: birds, livestock, wild animals, every swarming creature, and all humans.
verses.tsw_comparator: And all flesh died that moved upon the earth: birds and livestock and animals and every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth, and all humankind.

verses.rationale: Retain the dry-land scope and the nostril/breath echo of creation.
verses.before: Everything on the dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life died.
verses.after: Everything on dry land with the breath of life in its nostrils died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everything on the dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life died.

verses.rationale: Preserve destruction repetition and the limited remnant without adding a new moral explanation.
verses.before: He blotted out every living thing that was upon the face of the ground, from humankind to animals to creeping things and birds of the heavens. They were blotted out from the earth. Only Noah remained, and people who were with him in the ark.
verses.after: Every living thing on the ground was wiped out—humans, livestock, crawling creatures, and birds in the sky. They were wiped from the earth. Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: He blotted out every living thing that was upon the face of the ground, from humankind to animals to creeping things and birds of the heavens. They were blotted out from the earth. Only Noah remained, and those who were with him in the ark.

verses.rationale: Preserve the strength verb and 150-day duration distinct from forty days of rain.
verses.before: And the waters prevailed upon the earth one hundred fifty days.
verses.after: The waters continued to overwhelm the earth for 150 days.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the waters prevailed upon the earth one hundred fifty days.

subsequent_editorial_changes.previous_after: The waters held their power over the earth for 150 days.
subsequent_editorial_changes.rationale: Render the continuing force of gavar al naturally; retain the water subject, its prevailing force over the earth and the exact duration. The same root remains prominent in 7:18–20.

verses.rationale: Preserve remembered as action within relationship without suggesting prior forgetfulness; keep wind and animals in the turning point.
verses.before: Yet God remembered Noah and all the animals and all the livestock that were with him in the ark. And God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.
verses.after: God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and livestock with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God remembered Noah and all the animals and all the livestock that were with him in the ark. And God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.

verses.rationale: Retain the closing of both water sources and the separate stopping of rain.
verses.before: The fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the heavens was restrained.
verses.after: The springs of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky stopped.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fountains of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the heavens was restrained.

verses.rationale: Render the repeated motion idiom as gradual withdrawal without adding a new duration.
verses.before: And the waters receded steadily from the earth. At the end of one hundred fifty days the waters had diminished.
verses.after: The waters gradually withdrew from the earth. At the end of 150 days, they had diminished.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the waters receded steadily from the earth. At the end of one hundred fifty days the waters had diminished.

verses.rationale: Preserve the date and plural mountains rather than identify a single modern peak.
verses.before: In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat.
verses.after: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat.

verses.rationale: Separate ongoing withdrawal from the dated appearance of mountain summits.
verses.before: The waters continued to diminish until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
verses.after: The waters kept falling until the tenth month. On the first day of that month, the mountaintops became visible.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters continued to diminish until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.

verses.rationale: Preserve forty days and the explicit window; keep the action flowing into the raven's release.
verses.before: At the end of forty days Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
verses.after: After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of forty days Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.

verses.rationale: Retain the raven's repeated movement without asserting that it never returned.
verses.before: He sent out a raven, and it went to and fro until the waters were dried up from the earth.
verses.after: and released a raven. It flew back and forth until the waters on the earth dried up.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent out a raven, and it went to and fro until the waters were dried up from the earth.

verses.rationale: Name Noah to clarify the subject while preserving the purpose of the release.
verses.before: Then he sent out a dove from him, to see whether the waters had subsided from the face of the ground.
verses.after: Then Noah released a dove to find out whether the water had gone down from the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he sent out a dove from him, to see whether the waters had subsided from the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Keep the resting-foot image and all three receiving actions without turning them into an added devotional lesson.
verses.before: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, for the waters were still upon the face of all the earth. So he stretched out his hand and took her and brought her into the ark with him.
verses.after: The dove found nowhere to set its foot, because water still covered the whole earth, so it returned to Noah in the ark. He reached out, took it, and brought it back inside with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, for the waters were still upon the face of all the earth. So he stretched out his hand and took her and brought her into the ark with him.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated release and interval.
verses.before: He waited another seven days, and again he sent out the dove from the ark.
verses.after: He waited another seven days and released the dove from the ark again.
verses.tsw_comparator: He waited another seven days, and again he sent out the dove from the ark.

verses.rationale: Retain leaf rather than branch and the connection between observation and knowledge.
verses.before: The dove came back to him in the evening, and look, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in her mouth. So Noah knew that the waters had subsided from the earth.
verses.after: The dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in its beak. Noah knew then that the waters had gone down from the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The dove came back to him in the evening, and behold, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in her mouth. So Noah knew that the waters had subsided from the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve the second waiting interval and the final nonreturn.
verses.before: Then he waited another seven days and sent out the dove, and she did not return to him again.
verses.after: He waited another seven days and released the dove, but this time it did not return to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he waited another seven days and sent out the dove, and she did not return to him again.

verses.rationale: Retain all date components and distinguish surface drying from the later full dryness statement.
verses.before: In the six hundred first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and look, the face of the ground was dry.
verses.after: In Noah's 601st year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried from the earth. Noah removed the ark's covering and looked: the surface of the ground was dry.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the six hundred first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and behold, the face of the ground was dry.

verses.rationale: Retain the later date rather than collapse it into 8:13.
verses.before: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
verses.after: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was dry.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.

verses.rationale: Keep the divine speech introduction as a short transition.
verses.before: Then God spoke to Noah, saying,
verses.after: Then God spoke to Noah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then God spoke to Noah, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain the complete household in the command.
verses.before: “Go out from the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.
verses.after: “Leave the ark with your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go out from the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

verses.rationale: Keep all animal categories and the creation blessing echoes; record the written/read form in source extraction without treating it as an omitted verse.
verses.before: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh—birds and animals and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth—so that they may swarm upon the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth.”
verses.after: Bring out all the living creatures with you—birds, livestock, and everything that crawls on the earth. Let them teem across the earth, be fruitful, and multiply on it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh—birds and animals and every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth—so that they may swarm upon the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth.”

verses.rationale: Retain the source's family order, distinct from the command's order.
verses.before: So Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him.
verses.after: Noah left the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Noah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him.

verses.rationale: Preserve families rather than replace the term with species; keep the comprehensive inventory.
verses.before: Every animal, every creeping thing, every bird, everything that moves upon the earth, according to their families, went out from the ark.
verses.after: Every animal, every crawling creature, every bird—everything moving on the earth—left the ark by their families.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every animal, every creeping thing, every bird, everything that moves upon the earth, according to their families, went out from the ark.

verses.rationale: Keep clean selection and burnt offerings without substituting a generalized thanksgiving ritual.
verses.before: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD and took some of every clean animal and some of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
verses.after: Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every clean animal and every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD and took some of every clean animal and some of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

verses.rationale: Retain smell, divine inner speech, and human evil; note because/although force of ki rather than hiding the interpretive choice.
verses.before: And the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma. Then the LORD said in his heart, “I will never again curse the ground because of humankind, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Nor will I ever again strike down every living thing as I have done.
verses.after: The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma and said in his heart, “I will never again curse the ground because of humans, even though the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Never again will I strike down every living thing as I have done.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma. Then the LORD said in his heart, “I will never again curse the ground because of humankind, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Nor will I ever again strike down every living thing as I have done.

verses.rationale: Preserve all four paired rhythms and the conditional duration as poetry.
verses.before: While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, will not cease.”
verses.after: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will not cease.”
verses.tsw_comparator: While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease.”

verses.rationale: Keep the creation-blessing formula and the sons as addressees.
verses.before: Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
verses.after: God blessed Noah and his sons: “Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve the fear/dread pair, animal scope, and hand image rather than soften power into mere companionship.
verses.before: The fear of you and the dread of you will be upon every animal of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens, upon everything that creeps on the ground and upon all the fish of the sea. Into your hand they are given.
verses.after: Every wild animal, every bird in the sky, everything that moves on the ground, and all the fish in the sea will fear and dread you. They are given into your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every animal of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens, upon everything that creeps on the ground and upon all the fish of the sea. Into your hand they are given.

verses.rationale: Retain expanded food provision and the explicit comparison with plants.
verses.before: Every moving thing that lives will be food for you. As I gave you the green plants, I give you everything.
verses.after: Every moving creature that lives will be food for you. Just as I gave you green plants, I now give you everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you. As I gave you the green plants, I give you everything.

verses.rationale: Keep the apposition connecting life and blood, not a modern biological explanation.
verses.before: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you will not eat.
verses.after: But you must not eat flesh with its life—its blood—still in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But flesh with its life, that is, its blood, you shall not eat.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated demand, animals, human kinship, and the full value of the lifeblood clause.
verses.before: And for your lifeblood I will surely require an accounting. From every animal I will require it, and from humankind. From each person’s fellow human being I will require an accounting for human life.
verses.after: For your lifeblood I will demand an accounting. I will demand it from every animal and from every human; from each person's fellow human I will demand an accounting for human life.
verses.tsw_comparator: And for your lifeblood I will surely require an accounting. From every animal I will require it, and from humankind. From each one’s fellow human being I will require an accounting for human life.

verses.rationale: Retain the conventional by-a-human reading, violence, and divine-image rationale; note syntactic options without inserting a modern legal program.
verses.before: Whoever sheds human blood, by a human will that one’s blood be shed, for in the image of God he made humankind.
verses.after: Whoever sheds human blood, by a human shall that person's blood be shed, for God made humanity in God's image.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever sheds human blood, by a human shall that one’s blood be shed, for in the image of God he made humankind.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated multiplication rather than treat it as expendable redundancy.
verses.before: And you, be fruitful and multiply; abound upon the earth and multiply in it.”
verses.after: As for you, be fruitful and multiply. Teem across the earth and multiply on it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, be fruitful and multiply; abound upon the earth and multiply in it.”

verses.rationale: Keep both Noah and sons as the covenant speech audience.
verses.before: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him,
verses.after: God spoke to Noah and his sons who were with him:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him,

verses.rationale: Keep the present establishing and future generations as the beginning of the extended sentence.
verses.before: “As for me, look, I establish my covenant with you and with your offspring after you,
verses.after: “I am establishing my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
verses.tsw_comparator: “As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you and with your offspring after you,

verses.rationale: Retain the explicitly nonhuman covenant partners and repeated comprehensive scope.
verses.before: and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, all that came out of the ark, every animal of the earth.
verses.after: and with every living creature with you: birds, livestock, and every wild animal, all that came out of the ark—every living animal on earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, all that came out of the ark, every animal of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve covenant, cut-off language, all flesh, and the specific flood promise.
verses.before: I establish my covenant with you: never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood, and never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
verses.after: I establish my covenant with you: never again will all flesh be cut off by floodwaters. Never again will a flood destroy the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I establish my covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood, and never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth.”

verses.rationale: Retain the sign and repeated living-creature partners; keep the cross-verse introduction.
verses.before: God said, “This is the sign of the covenant that I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all generations:
verses.after: God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am giving between me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations to come:
verses.tsw_comparator: And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant that I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all generations:

verses.rationale: Keep bow rather than erase its wider Hebrew range; identify the rainbow setting and possible weapon resonance in a note.
verses.before: I have set my bow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
verses.after: I have set my bow in the clouds. It will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve the conditional appearance rather than make a separate promise detached from 9:15.
verses.before: When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the clouds,
verses.after: When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in them,
verses.tsw_comparator: When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow is seen in the clouds,

verses.rationale: Retain remember and the full covenant scope without removing the repeated all flesh.
verses.before: I will remember my covenant that is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh. And the waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
verses.after: I will remember my covenant with you and every living creature of all flesh. The waters will never again become a flood that destroys all flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will remember my covenant that is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh. And the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.

verses.rationale: Keep divine looking and remembering, everlasting, and the source's shift to God in the third person.
verses.before: When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.”
verses.after: When the bow is in the clouds, I will look at it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh on the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the concluding restatement and all-flesh partners.
verses.before: God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.”
verses.after: God told Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant I have established between me and all flesh on the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.”

verses.rationale: Keep the parentage note that prepares the later curse without shifting its recipient.
verses.before: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
verses.after: Noah's sons who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was Canaan's father.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Render the whole-earth population idiom naturally while keeping all three sons.
verses.before: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the entire earth was populated.
verses.after: These were Noah's three sons, and from them people spread across the whole earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was populated.

verses.rationale: Retain ground and vineyard while noting the possible Noah-the-farmer-began reading.
verses.before: Noah began to be a man of the soil, and he planted a vineyard.
verses.after: Noah began to work the ground and planted a vineyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Noah began to be a man of the soil, and he planted a vineyard.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three actions without adding motives or excusing drunkenness.
verses.before: He drank from the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself inside his tent.
verses.after: He drank some of its wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: He drank from the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself inside his tent.

verses.rationale: Keep saw nakedness without importing a speculative assault; retain the repeated Canaan parentage.
verses.before: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside.
verses.after: Ham, Canaan's father, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father and told his two brothers outside.

verses.rationale: Preserve the sequence and repeated refusal to look; do not replace the concrete scene with an abstract moral.
verses.before: Then Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it upon both their shoulders, and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were turned away, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.
verses.after: Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across their shoulders, and walked backward to cover their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned away, so they did not see him naked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it upon both their shoulders, and walked backward and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were turned away, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.

verses.rationale: Retain the vague done-to-him wording and younger/youngest ambiguity rather than invent an event.
verses.before: When Noah awoke from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him,
verses.after: When Noah awoke from his wine, he learned what his younger son had done to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Noah awoke from his wine and knew what his youngest son had done to him,

verses.rationale: Retain Canaan, not Ham, as the curse recipient and slave-of-slaves intensity; no racial category is present.
verses.before: he said, “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants will he be to his brothers.”
verses.after: He said, “Cursed be Canaan! He will be the lowest of slaves to his brothers.”
verses.tsw_comparator: he said, “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.”

verses.rationale: Preserve blessing of the LORD and the difficult plural pronoun rather than silently choose a narrower referent.
verses.before: And he said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem; and let Canaan be his servant.
verses.after: He also said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! Let Canaan be their slave.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem; and let Canaan be his servant.

verses.rationale: Retain the expansion wordplay and ambiguous he; note that God or Japheth may be the subject of dwelling.
verses.before: May God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be his servant.”
verses.after: May God give Japheth room to spread, and may he live in Shem's tents. Let Canaan be their slave.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May God enlarge Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be his servant.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the post-flood duration.
verses.before: Noah lived after the flood three hundred fifty years.
verses.after: Noah lived another 350 years after the flood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Noah lived after the flood three hundred fifty years.

verses.rationale: Retain the total and resume chapter 5's death refrain.
verses.before: Thus all the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and he died.
verses.after: Noah lived 950 years in all. Then he died.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus all the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and he died.

verses.rationale: Keep the three family lines and their post-flood timing.
verses.before: These are the generations of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
verses.after: This is the account of the families of Noah's sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.

verses.rationale: Preserve all seven names and their source order rather than force changes to names.
verses.before: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
verses.after: Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

verses.rationale: Retain the three-name Gomer line in the same readable formula.
verses.before: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
verses.after: Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

verses.rationale: Preserve the pinned Hebrew’s Dodanim form without silently harmonizing another passage.
verses.before: The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
verses.after: Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

verses.rationale: Make the spread intelligible while preserving land, language, clan, and nation categories.
verses.before: From these the coastland peoples spread into their lands, each according to its language, by their clans, in their nations.
verses.after: From these came the coastland peoples, spreading into their lands, each with its own language, organized by clans and nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: From these the coastland peoples spread into their lands, each according to its language, by their clans, in their nations.

verses.rationale: Keep the personal/ancestral names with Mizraim's Egypt connection explained in a note.
verses.before: The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
verses.after: Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.

verses.rationale: Preserve both generations and distinguish Seba from Sheba.
verses.before: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
